offer.say: Eleven adults, four metres of boards. They queue for the boards, {owner}. Kids just fall and get up. Grown-ups need something to hold, they just won't say it. Skate aids, the little push frames. We have none.

options.text: Can't they hold on to each other?
What about the chairs the kids use?
Those frames are pricey. Not this season.

each_other.say: They tried. Gary Pruett's cousin took out three people like a bowling ball. It was very social. It was not safe.

chairs.say: The kids' chairs are small. A grown man pushing a little chair looks like he's chasing it. They're embarrassed and then they don't come back. I want them to come back.

options.text: Then they'll have proper frames. Leave it with me.

decline.say: Okay. I'll keep rotating them along the boards like a car wash.

accepted.say: Thank you. And if you see the hall's orange chairs, those seven are the sturdy ones. Nobody knows why. I don't ask.

progress.say: How are we doing on things to hold?

options.text: I'll grab the orange chairs from upstairs.
I've got an idea about the stick barrel.
The frames are here. Next lesson?

p_barrel.say: Broken sticks? Oh, that's clever. Very gym teacher. I'm a little bit annoyed I didn't think of it.

p_lesson.say: Monday. I'll tell them there's new equipment. Adults love new equipment. They'll come just to look at it.

complete.say: Everybody on the ice at once. Nobody on the boards. Walter did a whole lap pushing a frame made of six Honest Hockey shafts and he said, 'It's a frame. It's a little heavy. It will be fine.' He'd read the label.

options.text: Lorne made them. He should hear that.
Can the kids use them too?
What happens to the orange chairs?

c_lorne.say: I'll write him a card. Gym teachers write very good cards. We have stickers.

c_kids.say: If they're not too heavy. I'll ask Lorne for a small one. A frame for a four-year-old out of a junior stick. He'll love that.

c_chairs.say: Back upstairs. I counted them. Still seven. Still orange. Still nobody knows.

done.say: Week six is the stop. They're ready. They don't know it yet.
